plan: In a second-price (Vickrey) auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of bidders or their strategies. This is because you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. With my value at $31, the optimal strategy is to bid exactly $31, ensuring I maximize expected profit without risk of overpaying.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. Since the winner pays the second-highest bid (not their own bid), there's no incentive to shade my bid up or down. Bidding exactly my value of $22 ensures I win whenever my value exceeds the market price (second-highest bid) and never overpay, maximizing expected profit. This is a single round with no history to adjust from, so truthful bidding is optimal.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the highest competing bid, and you pay only that competing bid, never more than your value. This holds regardless of the number of competitors or their bidding behavior. Since my value is $40, I should bid exactly $40 to maximize expected profit without risking overpaying or losing profitable opportunities.
